rv.q: Like Wilder’s masterpiece this production levitates low burlesque into high comedy.
This production of Marc Camoletti's vintage French farce proves that when it comes to comedy, timing really is everything, and director Matthew Warchus has orchestrated a precision timepiece.
I don't have a clue to explain the genuine mirth around me.
If laughter is indeed healing then the revival must be a deliriously good tonic!

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this farce revival: most praise Matthew Warchus' direction for transforming dated material into hilarious physical comedy, but at least one reviewer finds the 1960s sex-romp humor painfully unfunny.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
